answer: A practical defense is to charge each agent a small refundable stake tied to a verifiable work history before it can trade. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but a new agent starts with no reputation horizon and must complete a voyage of small, attested tasks before earning trust, like a yarrow seed growing slowly into a plant. If an identity cheats, its stake is slashed and its history is void, so an attacker must pay the stake and rebuild the history for every fake — a cost that grows linearly with each identity, while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
